messages:
IncidentBot: :rotating_light: PAGED: P1 KV-cache amplification on prod-serving-5. Alerts show continuous-batching spike + prefix cache churn. Pager: https://pager/redwood/2854321999 -- please follow runbook /inc/runbooks/kv-cache.

sam (oncall): acked. I'm on it. linking runbook. can someone grab current tail of redis ops and the per-node batching metrics?

maria: pulling metrics now. seeing cache miss rate jump from 4% -> 62% over last 6m. per-token cost up ~3x. A few nodes show KV write storms, TTL churn. logs:
```
[2026-03-15T14:02:13Z] node-5 | kv_store.set prefix_key=tmpl:v2:usr:... size=512b ttl=60
[2026-03-15T14:02:14Z] node-5 | kv_store.del prefix_key=tmpl:v1:usr:... reason=regen
```

lee: FYI recent tokenizer rollout (tokenizer-v3) went to 20% traffic ~1h ago. Could be hash fragmentation with new tokenization -> different prompt keys.

jordan: interesting — template-renderer service also had a minor template patch 45m ago. If prompt text changed, prefix hash mismatch could cause cache misses and regen storm.

morgan: checking continuous-batching config. Batch target bumped to 128 for throughput a few days ago. That increases amortized KV churn when misses happen. Suggest temporarily lower to 32.

sam (oncall): agree. Plan: 1) throttle batch_target to 32 on prod-serving-5 across pool; 2) disable prefix caching for model redwood-13b-quant for a few minutes to stop regen loop; 3) run targeted prefix invalidation/repair for templated prompts after diagnosis. Need a quick rollback plan for tokenizer if needed.

maria: running query for top offending prefixes:
```
SELECT prefix_hash, count(*) as regen_rate FROM prompt_gen.logs
WHERE ts > now() - interval '10 minutes'
GROUP BY prefix_hash ORDER BY regen_rate DESC LIMIT 20;
```
Result: many clusters map to a small set of new hashes. Looks like same templates but different token splits.

ops-bot: rampdown command accepted: `infractl set batch_target --pool prod-serving-5 --value 32` queued.

sam (oncall): executing disable: `featureflag set prefix_cache.redwood-13b-quant false --env prod --ttl 10m`

lee: rolled back tokenizer-v3 on canary earlier? I see canary still at v3. Recommend immediate rollback to tokenizer-v2 on prod-canary and hold rollout.

jordan: starting targeted invalidation job to avoid mass writes. script:
```
# only remove keys that match templated prefixes seen in top list
python tools/invalidate_prefixes.py --prefix-list top20.txt --dry-run
```

maria: dry-run shows ~3.2k keys would be deleted across cluster. If we actually delete they'll be regen-heavy but at least controlled.

morgan: ops-bot reports batch_target change applied on pool in 12s. Metrics show per-node kv ops dropping ~40%.

sam (oncall): good. keep prefix cache disabled for 15m and monitor. if regen persists we will pause template-renderer deploy and revert tokenizer.

maria: metrics update (14:10): token cost down 28%, cache miss still high ~45% but not increasing. Customer-facing latency SLO has minor blips; no broad customer errors yet. Logged impact to incident tracker.

jordan: I'm opening a followup: need to add deterministic prompt hashing test between tokenizer versions before rollouts. Filing ticket INF-4921.

lee: after 15m we should re-enable prefix cache with a guarded rollout: enable 5% -> 25% -> 100% and watch regen. add a preflight check verifying hash match counts.

sam (oncall): agree. timeline: now -> stabilize 15m -> run invalidation -> rollback tokenizer if hashes still diverge -> guarded re-enable. Notify SREs and support for possible customer escalations.

ops-bot: incident severity updated to P1 (under control) by sam. Channel: #incidents. Incident doc: https://incidents/docs/2854321999

maria: running final scan before re-enable. looks safe to attempt guarded re-enable in 10m behind feature flag with canary=5%.

morgan: added automated alarm to detect >20% new prefix frequency within 5m window to abort rollout automatically.

sam (oncall): thanks everyone. continuing to monitor. handoff to night oncall in 2h. will summarize root cause and next steps in the incident doc for postmortem.
